title: 第3章 武道境界第4章 安神
content_zh:
一声令下，数万新兵开始模仿。
江岳沉下心神，脑海中不断回放着教官每一个细微的发力点。
他按照第一式的要求，缓缓合拢双臂，试图寻找那种皮膜震动的感触。
然而，难。
极难。
他的动作显得僵硬且生涩，骨骼关节处不断发出不堪重负的嘎吱声。
那股温存在体内的气血，此刻像是一头不听使唤的倔驴，根本无法按照预定的路线去冲击表皮。
视网膜边缘，面板再次亮起。
【行为：锻体】
【状态：录入中……】
【当前进度：累积中……】
【评价：姿势偏差较多，气血传导滞塞，尚未触及皮膜真意。】
江岳并不气馁。
他一遍又一遍地调整着呼吸，配合着【顺气】词条，强行压制住筋肉的酸痛，一次次将自己塞入那个扭曲的姿势中。
独眼教官在高台上负手而立。
他的那只独眼如同冰冷的扫描仪，迅速掠过方阵。
他在寻找那些灵性。
武道修行，意志固然重要，但悟性往往决定了在那三个月内能走多远。
不远处，一名身形匀称的少年引起了他的注意。
那少年在短短数次尝试后，皮膜竟然已经隐隐泛起了一层红光，动作行云流水，显然极契合这套功法。

教官微微颔首，记下了对方的编号。
随后，他的目光扫到了江岳。
此前二十公里奔袭中，江岳表现还算不错。
但在这一刻，教官的眉头却微微皱起。
江岳的动作在他眼中，实在是太“死”了。
由于动作过于追求标准，反而显得呆板，缺乏那种气血流转的灵动感。
尤其是那单薄的体架，在执行那些大开大合的锻体动作时，显得有些力不从心。
看了三秒钟，教官便收回了视线，眼中的那一丝期待消失不见，取而代之的是一种意料之中的平淡。
“意志尚可，可惜根骨平平，悟性……亦不过中人之姿。”
他在心中给出了定论。
在这台庞大的战争机器里，有意志的凡人太多了，但最终能活下来的，往往是那些既有意志，又有天赋的怪物。
江岳并没有察觉到教官的失望，或者说，即便察觉到了，他也不在乎。
他在重复。
枯燥且机械的重复。
每当他的姿势偏离一分，视网膜上便会若隐若现地浮现出方才教官演武时的残影。
他在用这种最笨的办法，去强行校准自己的每一寸血肉。
天色渐暗。
content_en:
With an order, tens of thousands of new recruits began to imitate.
Jiang Yue calmed down and replayed every detail of the instructor's efforts in his mind.
Following the requirements of the first pose, he slowly closed his arms, trying to find the feeling of vibrating skin membranes.
However, it is difficult.
Extremely difficult.
His movements seemed stiff and jerky, and his bones and joints kept making overwhelming creaking sounds.
The warm qi and blood in the body are like a stubborn donkey that cannot be obeyed at this moment, unable to hit the epidermis according to the predetermined route.
At the edge of the retina, the panel lights up again.
[Behavior: Exercise]
[Status: Entering...]
[Current progress: Accumulating...]
[Evaluation: There are many posture deviations, qi and blood conduction is blocked, and the true meaning of the skin membrane has not yet been touched. 】
Jiang Yue was not discouraged.
He adjusted his breathing over and over again, matching the word "Shun Qi", forcibly suppressing the pain in his muscles, and pushed himself into that twisted posture again and again.
The one-eyed instructor stood on the high platform with his hands behind his back.
His one eye was like a cold scanner, quickly passing through the square array.
He was looking for those spirits.
In martial arts practice, will is important, but understanding often determines how far you can go in those three months.
Not far away, a well-proportioned young man caught his attention.
After just a few attempts, the young man's skin was already glowing with a faint red light, and his movements were smooth and fluid, which was obviously very suitable for this set of techniques.
The instructor nodded slightly and wrote down the other party's number.
Then, his eyes glanced at Jiang Yue.
In the previous 20-kilometer run, Jiang Yue performed pretty well.
But at this moment, the instructor's brows frowned slightly.
In his eyes, Jiang Yue's actions were too "dead".
Because the movements are too standard, they appear dull and lack the agility of the blood flow.
Especially the thin body frame seemed a little inadequate when performing those wide-opening and closing body-building movements.
After looking at it for three seconds, the instructor looked away. The trace of expectation in his eyes disappeared, replaced by an expected dullness.
"The willpower is acceptable, but it's a pity that the bones are mediocre, and the understanding...is only average."
He made a conclusion in his mind.
In this huge war machine, there are too many willed mortals, but the ones who survive in the end are often the monsters who have both will and talent.
Jiang Yue didn't notice the instructor's disappointment, or in other words, even if he did, he didn't care.
He is repeating.
Boring and mechanical repetition.
Every time his posture deviated even a little, the afterimage of the instructor's martial arts performance would vaguely appear on his retina.
He is using this stupidest method to forcefully calibrate every inch of his flesh and blood.
It's getting dark.
